description:
## Problem

Reach has a Jason plugin that classifies maps passed to Jason.encode!/2 as external payload contracts. Catseye should detect when tainted data is serialized via Jason.encode! and sent over HTTP — this is a data exfiltration vector.

## Evidence

From reach:
- reach/lib/reach/plugins/poison.ex: Poison effect classifier
- reach/lib/reach/visualize.ex: Jason.encode!(graph) — sends internal data over HTTP
- Multiple modules use @derive Jason.Encoder for external data contracts

## Expected Behavior

Jason.encode!/Poison.encode! with tainted data flowing into HTTP responses should be flagged as potential data exfiltration. This is a lower-priority concern than SSRF/CommandInjection but worth tracking.

## Suggested Fix

This is more of a taint-tracking improvement than a rule addition. The SSRF rules already detect HTTP client calls. The missing piece is tracking that Jason.encode!(tainted_data) flowing into HTTP response bodies. Consider adding Jason.encode!/Jason.decode! as transform sinks that preserve taint.
title: Elixir: add Jason/Poison encode/decode as SSRF sink boundary
